hook: A developer broke down Opus 5.5's 4 breaking changes before they could wreck his agent in production
caption:
Claude Opus 5.5 just landed, cheaper than Opus 5 and beating GPT-6 Astra on coding benchmarks ⚡

Anthropic's new model is faster and cheaper per token than Opus 5 — but it also changes how tool calls and extended thinking work under the hood.

→ thinking can no longer be turned off
→ some forced tool-use calls that used to work now error out
→ thinking blocks are now tied to a specific model and conversation
→ the old computer_20251124 tool gets rejected

Which one of these would've broken your agent first? 👇

youtube.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 just launched — cheaper than Opus 5 and ahead of GPT-6 Astra on Terminal-Bench, but it breaks 4 things that worked before.

Here's what changed: extended thinking can't be disabled, some forced tool-use calls now error, thinking blocks are tied to a specific model and conversation, and the old computer_20251124 tool is rejected.

If you're running Claude in production, check your code before you upgrade.
